headline: Not yet. Basket reads 74; the IMF ranks an AI correction a top risk.
summary: The first scored basket puts indicator pressure at 73.6: valuations sit beyond any prior burst while rates and credit stay calm. The S&P 500 closed flat on Tuesday 13 October as chips fell a fifth day and the IMF named an AI correction a top risk. [1][3]

analysis: The basket scores 73.6: fragility 86.0, trigger 39.1, confirmation 87.6. Price to sales at 3.85, household equities at 48.2% of financial assets and subprime auto delinquency at 6.13% sit beyond any prior burst; the Shiller CAPE at 41.84, TSMC revenue growth of 54.6% and hyperscaler capex at 96% of operating cash flow score above 90. The Nasdaq trades at 3.49 times the S&P 500, chips at 1.56 times, and margin debt is up 37% in a year. [6][7][8][9][10][11][17][19][20][21][25]

The triggers are calm: the BIS credit gap is −11.3 points, the Fed has cut 25bp in a year to a 3.75–4% target and the high-yield spread is 311bp, though the 10-year yield at 5.21% is not. Unemployment at 4.2% and an NFCI of −0.49 confirm nothing yet. Wall Street closed Tuesday 13 October flat: the S&P 500 lost 0.02% to 7,805.45 and the Nasdaq 0.15%, while the PHLX chip index fell a fifth straight session, over 8% in the run. Seoul's Kospi dropped 5.46%. [1][5][12][13][14][15][16][18]

The IMF's stability report named an AI-driven correction one of three salient risks and counted $300 billion of equity and $650 billion of debt in 14 circular AI deals since 2023; hyperscalers now issue 10% of global investment-grade bonds. BofA found 37% of fund managers overweight tech, most since August 2020. Against that, FactSet's forward P/E of 19.1 equals its 10-year average. Why 78: the basket anchors lower at 73.6, but the IMF warning and a fifth day of chip losses hold the score. [1][2][3][4][26]
